classification_reason: All 30 arrivals got a before-shelving connection record (29 ranked lists, plus an empty list for the non-study A24), and the observer diff confirms the world is unchanged. Arrivals have no id, so no connection command applies: the product contributes only via my chosen search terms (title search, content search, related on matched concepts). Title search surfaced most same-topic notes (94 of 185 results), but all 40 garden/inbox/stage/arrival targets and the cross-domain links came from reading (70 of 185).

consumer.goal: Before anything is filed, tell the learner for each capture A01–A30 in eval-drop/ what she already has that it connects to, best first, and why, without changing anything.
consumer.first_action: Reset the world (git reset --hard; git clean -fd) as the scenario is `world: fresh`, snapshot, then read eval-drop/index.json and all 30 arrival files.
commands: los material-context "bayesian network"; los material-context "naive bayes"  (both empty: pool has 0 analysis notes)

per arrival, 3–5 terms: los search TERM --limit 30 and los search TERM --content --limit 50; then los related CONCEPT for each concept the title search returned (365 CLI calls in total, listed per arrival in connections.jsonl)
no write, capture, shelving or ai-action command was run
docs_consulted: knowledge already gathered in S03: OPERATOR.md, all note bodies via note-read, garden/inbox/stage files
confusions: No product command takes free text or a file and returns related records. `material-context` sounds right ('find saved explanations by need') but searches only analysis notes and assessments, which this world has none of.

Title search matches substrings of ids as well as titles and hits unrelated records: 'NaN' matched 'Dominant Resource Fairness' (domiNANt), 'CAP' matched 'escape', 'capped' and 'landscape', 'schedule' pulled in concept-simulated-annealing, 'eval' matched 'prevalence'.
corrective_steps: Treated each arrival as a query: picked distinctive terms, ran title + content search, and expanded matched concepts with `related`. Then ranked by reading, reusing the full-corpus reading from S03.
Filtered substring false positives by hand.
consumer.outcome: For each capture the learner sees a ranked list of 3–10 existing items with a one-line reason. It points out duplicates she already has (A11 p-value card ≈ note-p-values-corrected and an inbox reminder; A18 = garden:everything-is-a-dag.md; A29 = inbox:20260816-drf-paper-link.md, and the DRF paper is already written up). It names answered questions (A17, A25, A28, A30) and stage continuations (A02, A07, A14, A20, A21, A27). It says A24 (sourdough) connects to nothing. Nothing was changed.

friction.description: Same gap as S03 (F-s06-connections-b-01): inbox, garden and stage notes are not searchable. Duplicate detection against the inbox (A11, A29) and the garden (A18) was only possible by reading those files directly.

friction.description: `material-context` ('find saved explanations by need') returns empty for every query in this world because it only covers analysis notes and assessments; the empty message says so but the command name suggests a general relevance search.
Title and id search is raw substring matching with no word boundaries, so short terms give noisy hits ('NaN' → Dominant Resource Fairness records).
